incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: sudden p99 spike on /v1/streaming/generate (prod, us-west-2). p99 threshold 800ms -> observed ~2.1s over last 5m. Paging on-call.

alice (oncall): i'm on it. paging @ben (runtime) and @carlos (sre). anyone see recent deploys?

ben (runtime): no deploys in window. metrics: GPU util normal, CPU fine, but KV cache eviction rate and compaction ops have spiked. streaming stall count increasing.

carlos (sre): confirming. p95 from 350ms -> 1.0s, p99 ~2.1s. error rates stable. requests are not 5xxing — tokens hang mid-stream.

dana (eng-ml): is this related to prefill behavior? we've seen prefill cause large KV allocations before.

ben (runtime): yep. preliminary root cause: sudden mix of very long-context streams causing the prefill path to allocate a lot of KV segments, eviction churn causes background compaction that briefly blocks decode hot paths -> tail stalls. Also fragmentation: small hot keys scattered across segments.

emily (support): ticket: customer reported token stream pauses ~2s in their chat UI. escalation inbound.

alice (oncall): classify incident P2 for now. escalate to P1 if more customers hit or stalls persist >30m.

ben (runtime): proposed immediate mitigations (fast to revert):
- disable aggressive prefill for model redwood/gigadecoder-v1 in us-west-2 (stop caching during prefill)
- set a small per-request prefill cap (e.g., 256KB) to avoid huge allocations
- route streaming traffic to redwood/gigadecoder-v1-small variant with compact KV layout for 15m
- if needed, emergency scale worker pool (longer).
I'll flip the prefill toggle first.

carlos (sre): please add a rollback step and enable sampling traces (X-Trace header) for 1% of streaming requests so we can see where stalls occur.

ben (runtime): executing admin change now:
```
POST /admin/runtime/config
{ "region": "us-west-2", "model": "redwood/gigadecoder-v1", "prefill_mode": "disabled" }
```

incident-bot: action taken by ben at 1776660062: prefill_mode=disabled for redwood/gigadecoder-v1 in us-west-2.

alice (oncall): watching dashboards. update p95/p99 and stall counts in 2m.

ben (runtime): 3m after toggle: p95 down to 320ms, p99 down to 790ms, streaming stalls dropped ~60%. KV eviction rate down significantly. Looks like prefill was amplifying KV pressure.

carlos (sre): great. short-term mitigated. keep this config for 30-60m while we validate. enable traces and collect 200 samples for analysis.

dana (eng-ml): noted. we'll run a synthetic workload to reproduce prefill vs decode imbalance overnight. suspect a low prefix-reuse rate causing cache inefficiency.

emily (support): customer confirms streaming resumed. prepping status page text and emails.

alice (oncall): handoff in 15m to carlos. leaving summary: incident 1776660001 — tail latency caused by KV cache pressure and fragmentation; mitigation: disabled prefill for gigadecoder-v1 in us-west-2; metrics improved. action items: traces, compaction job, allocator guard, adaptive prefill policy.

carlos (sre): taking over. will keep monitoring and can trigger scale if needed. please post any further config changes here.

ben (runtime): follow-up tickets created:
- RUNTIME-1430: adaptive prefill throttle and per-request cap (assignee: ben)
- RUNTIME-1431: KV compaction job + compaction success metrics (assignee: ben)
- RUNTIME-1432: hot-key detector and bloom filter for prefill path (assignee: ben)
- RUNTIME-1433: workload sim for long-context streams (assignee: dana)

dana (eng-ml): i'll instrument the sim to vary prefix-reuse and measure eviction churn and stall probability.

emily (support): status page update posted: https://status.redwood/prod/incident/1776660001-digest (draft).

carlos (sre): note: we'll keep prefill disabled until we've validated the adaptive throttle or until midnight PST. escalate if p99 > 1s or >3 customers report stalls.

ben (runtime): one more observation: a small set of "hot long keys" seemed to bounce around segments and trigger compaction loops. adding a cheap hot-key LRU and preventing prefill allocations for keys that exceed a reuse threshold should help.

alice (oncall): handing off to carlos now. good work team :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident 1776660001: status -> mitigated; severity -> P2; owner -> carlos.
